observation.description: On @expo/snapback-react 0.1.7, a provider that owns any active live-query subscription never brings its managed presence room out of 'connecting': the presence state stays 'stale' with publisher 'publishing' indefinitely, while remote deltas still arrive into the wedged room. A presence-only provider on the same session works immediately (ready/published, both personas visible). Explicit provider connectionId does not help. The headless subscribeEphemeral overlay path multiplexes fine with concurrent live queries, so this is React-provider room readiness, not the ephemeral lane. Consequence: the documented one-provider App pattern (queries + useSnapbackPresence together, exactly what clients/react.md teaches) cannot show presence at all in a chat UI.

competitorOutcome.description: Convex core has no native ephemeral presence at all (two explicit GAPs in the frozen chat arm), so Snapback's native presence is the differentiator — but only if the first-party React surface can actually render it beside live queries. The frozen evidence has no competitor React-presence baseline to lose to; the loss is against Snapback's own headless arm.

mustNotRegress: The headless overlay contract (register-before-snapshot, TTL pruning, granted-id provenance) and the provider's zero-leak disposal, both of which pass today.
smallestCoherentFix: Make the provider's presence room readiness proof correct when the managed socket is already open and owned by live-query demand (the room must observe existing socket readiness rather than waiting for a fresh transition), with a regression test that opens one provider with a live query and a managed presence value together.
acceptanceWitness: A single prepared provider with one live query observer and one managed presence value reaches presence status 'ready' with publisher 'published' within the collection dispatch budget, on the packaged public closure.
